newsitem.title: USA: Bliley asks Clinton to help reform Superfund.
newsitem.headline: Bliley asks Clinton to help reform Superfund.

text.p: House Commerce Committee chairman Thomas Bliley, Republican of Virginia, called on President Clinton to use his State of the Union address early next year to make a proposal to reform the Superfund law for cleaning up toxic waste.

Bliley said the fees that pay for toxic waste cleanups are expiring and Rep. Bill Archer, a Republican of Texas, "has assured me that they will not be renewed unless there is reform of the underlying structure." Archer is chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee.

"The president knows full well that there is not enough money to clean the system up in the existing trust fund without continuation of these fees," Bliley told the American Enterprise Institute. "So I fully expect some movement."

"Bill Clinton identified toxic waste cleanups as a priority in his last State of the Union message. I'm looking forward to his proposal in his upcoming State of the Union message, in January," Bliley said.
Republicans say they want to streamline the Superfund, by speeding up cleanups and spending less on litigation.
Bliley said Superfund had already spent $15 billion on some 90 sites and there are some 1,300 sites left to go.

Bliley said Republicans would offer their own legislation regardless of what Clinton does, but they would prefer a bipartisan approach. He said Democrat John Dingell of Michigan has pledged to work with him "in a bipartisan fashion."
Bliley, who was discussing his committee's agenda for next year, also said deregulation of the electricity generating industry would be a top priority and "may be our most ambitious agenda item."
He said some electric companies say it's a question of state's rights, but he felt there had to be a federal role.
